## The task

The box starts at rest on the floor and must end fully on the platform, at
rest. The disk alone cannot carry it. The **indirect lift** tips the box onto
the step corner, lets the disk walk round to the box's raised underside,
lifts the box off the floor and rolls it onto the platform, the box held at
every instant:

{g} → {m<sub>x</sub>, g} → {m<sub>x</sub>, g, s} ⇒ {m<sub>x</sub>,
g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} → {g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} →
{m<sub>z</sub>, g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} → {m<sub>z</sub>,
s<sub>v</sub>} → {m<sub>z</sub>, t} → (transport) goal.

## The planner finds it from the scene alone

The search is given the scene and the goal, nothing else: every edit the gate
admits except releases, transports toward the gate's targets, and outcome
children (a call's child is the state it reached). Every dynamic outcome is
rejected, so every solve is **held**. The motions are the quasi-static
realizer Λ<sub>qs</sub> in MuJoCo. Both test sets are held out (never used
for training) and run at the band's two ends μ = 0.3 and 0.5, each search up
to 192 calls: 100 random lift starts (F1 seed 13), 200 searches; and the
original test set, the canonical start (the disk 10 cm from the box) and 16
random lift starts (F1 seed 11), 34 searches. The ordering is V₁ + the learned
ranker π (round 1), with V₀'s measured edge lengths.

| Held-out set | μ = 0.3 | μ = 0.5 | All (Wilson 95%) | Calls to solve (mean / median) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 random starts (F1 seed 13) | 94 / 100 | 99 / 100 | **193 / 200** (96.5%; 93–98%) | 89 / 91 |
| Original: canonical + 16 (F1 seed 11) | 16 / 17 | 17 / 17 | **33 / 34** (97%; 85–99%) | 88 / 91 |

Every solve is held and is the indirect lift; some hold the box by its lower
corner instead of its underside (16 of the 193, one of the 33). Of the 7
failures among the 200, 6 run out of actions to try and one reaches the
192-call budget. The canonical start takes 86 calls at μ = 0.3 (11 on the
path) and 94 at μ = 0.5 (12). The original set's one failure (seed 11, start
14, μ = 0.3) reaches the budget.

**With the simulator corrected.** These searches run with MuJoCo's
EULERDAMP flag disabled, so MJX integrates the solved acceleration. With it
on, MJX integrated a force sum that an unconverged contact solve could turn
into a kick of a box at rest. On the same machines, the earlier runs solved
192 of 200 and 33 of 34: 8 earlier failures are now solved and 7 earlier
solves are not (exact McNemar p = 1). Replayed call by call, three of the
earlier failures come from such a kick (one of them the first push, which
flipped the box upside down), two earlier solves relied on the box's creep at
rest failing a call, and the others part at falls that end differently or at
float-level differences that grow along the search.

**Round 2 of V₁ and π**, trained on 408 searches (seeds 20–29), ranks better
offline (V₁'s Spearman correlation 0.87 → 0.93, π's top-1 84% → 94%) but
solved exactly the same searches as round 1 with EULERDAMP on: 192 of 200 and
33 of 34 on the same machines (exact McNemar p = 1), with 88 calls to solve
against 89 (not re-measured with EULERDAMP off). The failures were exhausted
candidate sets, not ordering failures: on these starts, ordering is saturated.

**The configuration** (the defaults of `master`):

- transition poses must be admissible: no disk target buried in the box;
- transports aim inside their target sets by δ = 10 mm (the δ-erosion);
- the box's rotation range is ±180° (a ±90° joint stop could carry load);
- each approach is checked by the gate's hold test with the disk's own force, and refused before
  the disk moves if it would tip the box (the same 33 are solved with the same calls without it);
- unhinted search, dynamic outcomes rejected, 192 calls;
- EULERDAMP disabled: MJX integrates the solved acceleration;
- V₁ and π of round 1, V₀ with edge lengths measured from logged calls.

**V₀** is the weighted graph distance to the goal plus a pose term
([how it is built](../planar-build/search.qmd#v0)); its edge lengths come from
the calls of round 0's training searches (a transfer succeeds 46% of the time, a
break 69%).
**V₁ and π** are learned by fitted value iteration and the LTS loss from
unhinted searches on other starts (F1 seeds 20–22, never the test set), in two
rounds: 80 searches of 64 calls, then 48 of 192 calls run with round 0's V₁ and
π. V₁ enters only the search's order; acceptance stays with V₀.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Previous configuration (±90° rotation stop, admissible poses off)

Measured on the same 34 searches with the box's rotation stopped at ±90°, no
admissibility filter on transition poses, EULERDAMP on and, unless stated, no
δ-erosion. V₀
alone and round 0 were not re-measured in the configuration above.

| Ordering | Erosion | All | Calls to solve (mean) |
|---|---|---|---|
| V₀ + uniform ranker | no | 17 / 34 | 154 |
| V₁ + π, round 0 | no | 23 / 34 | 142 |
| V₁ + π, round 1 | no | 26 / 34 | 89 |
| V₁ + π, round 1, V₀ measured lengths | no | 28 / 34 | 88 |
| V₀ + uniform ranker | yes | 26 / 34 | 139 |
| V₁ + π, round 1 | yes | 33 / 34 | 87 |

In both settings the learned pair solves every search V₀ solves and more
(exact McNemar p = 0.004 without erosion, 0.016 with it), with 42–50% fewer
calls where both solve. Without erosion, of the 8 searches round 1 left
unsolved, 7 ran out of actions to try; with 64 calls none of 18 was solved: the
search reached {m<sub>z</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} with the box at 51–57°, where
Λ<sub>qs</sub> refuses the roll, and the longer searches found a re-grip
(break m<sub>z</sub> to 63°, make m<sub>z</sub>).
:::

### Clips

Each clip replays the search's solution call by call on the processor that
ran the search (AMD EPYC 9334), and every call reproduces the log bit for bit.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How to read a clip

- **View.** From the side, with +x to the **left**, as in the paper. The
  green surface is the platform, the grey one the floor, the blue ball the
  disk. A red stripe marks the face the box rests on at the start.
- **Caption bar.** The run; the current edit *k/n* with its formations
  (σ → σ′); the call's outcome and the state it reached; the phase; the
  formation the recognizer reads right now; and whether the replay matched
  the log.
- **Speed.** The badge at the top left states it. The path plays as one
  motion: in real time while the box or the disk moves, easing to 3× while
  both rest. A call's outcome stays on screen while the next call plays.
- **Card.** The last frame carries the search's summary.
:::

## With the formation sequence given

In the previous configuration (with EULERDAMP on), given the indirect lift's sequence as a hint
(at a node in the chain's k-th formation only edits into the (k+1)-th and
transports), the planner with V₀ with equal edge lengths and the uniform ranker
solves at μ = 0.5 (15 calls, 12 on the path) and exhausts its search at μ =
0.3 and 0.4: the branch that would succeed depends on where a push ends to
within a degree (break m<sub>x</sub> from 43.1° succeeds, from 43.8° it does
not), and the hint leaves no other way. With V₀'s measured edge lengths, the
hinted search solves at μ = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 (15, 13 and 15 calls), on the
routes of the paper. The clip below is from that configuration and an
earlier renderer, which holds each call's last frame.

<video src="media/indirect/hinted_v0it0_mu0.5.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

## What this shows, and what it does not

- **The lift, found and held, at both ends of the friction band**, from the
  scene and the goal alone, on starts the learned parts never saw.
- **One scene, one task.** The step and the box; other scenes (the families)
  are not run.
- **Budget.** 7 of 200 searches (and 1 of 34) fail within 192 calls; 6 of
  the 8 run out of actions to try.
- **The realizer.** Λ<sub>qs</sub> plans held poses, not stick–slip plans
  ([the local solver](../planar-build/local-solver.qmd#qs-slip)).

## Configuration and reproduction

The searches ran at c-gnn commit `1917e2e` (`master` with EULERDAMP disabled
in the scene files), on Juno's compute nodes; results and the comparison with
the earlier runs: `cmg/scripts/step4/chain_search/results/noeulerdamp`. V₀:
`cmg/scripts/step4/value/results/v0_it1`. V₁ and π:
`cmg/scripts/step4/chain_search/results/night_2026-11-13/model_v1pi_it1`.
Searches run on CPU, one per 3 cores; a search needs about 80–90 thousand
memory mappings (`CMG_MAPGUARD` must allow them). All 234 searches ran on
Juno's compute nodes (AMD EPYC 9334, 262,144 mappings per process).
From `cmg/`:

```text
CMG_DISK_FRICTION=0.3 CMG_MAPGUARD=0 JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu PYTHONPATH=src .venv314/bin/python \
    scripts/step4/chain_search/run_chain.py OUT --no-hint --dynamic-outcomes reject --budget 192 \
    --v0 scripts/step4/value/results/v0_it1/v0_it1.json \
    --v1 scripts/step4/chain_search/results/night_2026-11-13/model_v1pi_it1 \
    --learned-pi scripts/step4/chain_search/results/night_2026-11-13/model_v1pi_it1 \
    --seed 11 --index 12
#   without --seed/--index: the canonical start; CMG_DISK_FRICTION=0.5: the band's other end
#   admissible transition poses, the delta-erosion and the approach check are on by default
```
